shell-settings.title: Settings
shell-settings.pane-failed: This pane couldn’t open. The others still work.
shell-settings.pane.general.lede: Where files open, where you take over, and how tasks start.
shell-settings.editor.hint: File links in cards and diffs
shell-settings.terminal.hint: Where you carry on a task yourself: a terminal inside wisp, or a terminal app
shell-settings.tui.hint: Each task you send opens straight in the agent’s own terminal, already working on your prompt, instead of wisp’s cards. Follow-ups are typed there, and opening the task again resumes it
shell-settings.blocks.hint: Agents end with wisp’s cards: diffs, test runs, previews, next steps. Off, they answer in plain text, which also reads cleaner when you take over
shell-settings.worktree.hint: Each task gets its own branch from origin/main, in git repos
shell-settings.review.hint: Before you merge a task’s PR, a harness other than the one that wrote it reads the diff and lists what it would fix, and the tests run again on the PR’s head. Merge stays possible; it says when the PR isn’t reviewed or the review found issues. Runs on that harness’s own account, never another
shell-settings.fix-conflicts.hint: Without waiting for a click on Fix conflicts: when a shipped PR conflicts with its base, the task merges the base in, resolves it and pushes
shell-settings.read-times.hint: A prompt that starts with a time (“in 5 min …”, “tomorrow at 9 …”) or says “remind me … in 1 hour” is scheduled for then. A chip under the box shows the time before you send
shell-settings.watch.hint: On long tasks, agents may put a page beside the task that shows their progress as they go, and keep it current. It opens in the side panel
shell-settings.apps.hint: Agents may answer with a small page you use in place, like a slider with a live preview or a list to pick from. It runs sandboxed, with no network, and sends nothing until you click Send
shell-settings.transcript.hint: Every message and step the agent took, with its presentation at the end. Any one card switches with its Transcript button or V
shell-settings.pane.appearance.lede: Light or dark, on this computer and every device that opens it.
shell-settings.theme.hint: System follows your computer’s light or dark setting
shell-settings.pane.notifications.lede: Hear about questions and finished tasks, here or on your phone.
shell-settings.notify.blocked: Blocked — allow notifications for this site in your browser
shell-settings.phone.hint: Questions and finished tasks on your phone, through the wisp app
shell-settings.channels.hint: Send “on laptop fix the login” to wisp on Cloud, with this computer’s name, and it starts a task here: Plan unless you ask, Edits at most, never Full auto. Only this computer can turn this on
shell-settings.pane.keys.lede: Keys work when you’re not typing in a box. ⌘K opens search and commands from anywhere.
shell-settings.keys.last: Last task: tap to jump back, hold Ctrl and Tab through the list
shell-settings.keys.takeover: Take over: carry on with the agent in a terminal
shell-settings.keys.shell: Shell in the task’s folder (again: back to the reply box)
shell-settings.keys.pr: Review PR: checks, reviews and comments in the side panel
shell-settings.keys.changes: Changes: every file the task changed, in the side panel
shell-settings.keys.rerun: Rerun with another harness, model or thinking level
shell-settings.keys.fork: Fork: a new task that carries on from here, on its own branch
shell-settings.keys.ship: Ship it: commit, push and open a PR (worktree tasks)
shell-settings.keys.history: Earlier prompts (in an empty prompt box)
shell-settings.keys.feedback: Send feedback to the wisp team (in any prompt box)
shell-settings.keys.bug: Report a bug in wisp (in any prompt box)
shell-settings.pane.diagnostics.lede: What this page knows about its computers, commands and flows. A bug report can carry it.
